vin_find_help_link: Where can I find my VIN?
vin_find_help_intro: Your VIN is a unique 17-character code for your vehicle. Check these four common places:
vin_find_loc_dashboard_desc: Stand outside on the driver's side. Look at the lower-left corner of the windshield — on the dashboard edge you'll see a small metal or plastic plate with the VIN printed on it.
vin_find_loc_door_desc: Open the driver's door. On the door frame (the metal edge the door closes against) there is a white or silver sticker with the VIN, build date, and tire pressure info.
vin_find_loc_documents_desc: Your vehicle registration, title certificate, or bill of sale lists the VIN in the vehicle identification section — look for a field labeled "VIN" or "Vehicle ID Number".
vin_find_loc_insurance_desc: Your auto insurance card, policy document, or insurer app lists the VIN alongside the year, make, and model of the vehicle.
vin_find_help_tip: A valid VIN is exactly 17 characters.
vin_find_alt_dashboard: VIN plate on the dashboard viewed through the windshield
vin_find_alt_door: VIN sticker on the driver door frame
vin_find_alt_documents: Vehicle registration document showing the VIN

country_usa_description: The US runs one of the world's largest used-car markets — millions of sales across 50 states. Sellers don't always share the full story. Verify before you buy.
country_usa_issue_0: Salvage & rebuilt titles — hidden by cross-state transfers
country_usa_issue_1: Hurricane and flood damage — common in Florida, Louisiana, Texas
country_usa_issue_2: Odometer rollback — common in older US imports
country_usa_issue_3: Lemon law buybacks — never declared by dealers
country_usa_included_0: Auction & marketplace records across all 50 states
country_usa_issues_sub: The most common red flags we find on US-market vehicles — before you commit to a purchase.
country_usa_included_sub: Every report pulls from auction houses, insurance filings, and provider databases across all 50 states.
country_usa_included_note: Data is sourced directly from providers — we do not estimate or fabricate records.
country_usa_faq_0_a: A salvage title means the vehicle was declared a total loss by an insurance company. A rebuilt title means it was repaired and re-registered. Both are significant red flags.
country_usa_faq_1_q: How does flood damage get hidden?
country_usa_faq_1_a: Vehicles flood-damaged in one state are often transported to another state and retitled, erasing the damage history. Our multi-state search catches this.
country_usa_faq_2_q: Where is the VIN on a US car?
country_usa_faq_2_a: On US vehicles, the VIN is on the driver's side dashboard (visible through the windshield) and on the driver's side door jamb sticker.
country_korea_description: South Korea has 25M+ registered vehicles and a fast-moving used market. Hidden damage and undisclosed history are common. Check before you buy or import.
country_korea_issue_0: Hidden accident repairs — unmatched paint and filler
country_korea_issue_1: Odometer manipulation — extremely common in used cars registered in South Korea
country_korea_issue_2: Import compliance issues — left/right-hand drive conversions
country_korea_issue_3: Undisclosed water damage — from heavy Korean monsoons
country_korea_included_4: Theft & loss records from insurance filings
country_korea_issues_sub: Real risks in the Korean used-car market — especially for imports and private sales.
country_korea_included_sub: Regional sources including Encar, insurance filings, and Korean marketplace listings.
country_korea_included_note: Insurance claim payouts are shown separately from structural accident history — so you see the full picture.
country_korea_faq_0_q: Are cars registered in South Korea safe to buy or import?
country_korea_faq_0_a: Yes, when properly checked. South Korea has a large used-car market with all brands — domestic and imported. Undisclosed damage and odometer fraud are known risks. Our report gives you the full picture.
country_korea_faq_1_q: Where is the VIN on a Korean car?
country_korea_faq_1_a: Korean VINs start with 'K' and are found on the dashboard near the windshield and on the engine block. Some older models have them on the firewall.
country_korea_faq_2_q: What data sources do you use for Korea?
country_korea_faq_2_a: We aggregate data from Korean auction platforms (such as Encar and K Car), private insurance filings, Facebook Marketplace, and used-car listing databases to compile a comprehensive vehicle history.
country_canada_description: Canada has 30M+ registered vehicles and a busy used-car market from coast to coast. Branded titles, hidden insurance claims and cross-province transfers are common risks. Verify before you buy or import.
country_canada_issue_0: Branded & rebuilt titles — hidden by inter-provincial transfers
country_canada_issue_1: Winter salt and rust damage — often undisclosed in private sales
country_canada_issue_2: Insurance write-offs relisted without full disclosure
country_canada_issue_3: US flood cars imported and retitled in Canada
country_canada_issues_sub: The most common red flags on Canadian used vehicles — before you hand over a deposit.
country_canada_included_sub: Every report pulls auction data, insurance indicators and registration signals across Canadian provinces and territories.
country_canada_included_note: Data is sourced directly from providers — we do not estimate or fabricate records.
country_canada_faq_0_q: What is a branded title in Canada?
country_canada_faq_0_a: A branded title marks a vehicle that was written off, rebuilt, or declared irreparable by an insurer or provincial authority. It is a major warning sign for buyers.
country_canada_faq_1_q: Can US flood cars be hidden in Canada?
country_canada_faq_1_a: Yes. Flood-damaged US vehicles are sometimes imported and sold in Canada with incomplete history. Our cross-border VIN search helps surface prior damage records.
country_canada_faq_2_q: Where is the VIN on a Canadian car?
country_canada_faq_2_a: Canadian VINs often start with '2' and appear on the driver's dashboard (visible through the windshield), the driver's door jamb, and on ownership documents.

help_subtitle: Quick answers to the most common questions about kmcheck.
help_faq_1_q: Where do I find my VIN number?
help_faq_1_a: Your 17-character VIN is on the driver's side dashboard (visible through the windshield), the driver's door jamb sticker, your vehicle title, insurance card, or registration documents.
help_faq_2_a: What appears in a report depends on the VIN and market. Some reports include a wide range of records — mileage history, accidents, salvage or title brands, theft records, ownership changes, and photos when available. Others include fewer sections; many still show at least mileage and/or accident records when those exist in our sources. A report is not the car's full lifetime history — it shows what we could find from our data providers for that VIN at the time of your check.
help_faq_3_q: How long does a report take?
help_faq_3_a: Most reports are delivered within seconds after payment is confirmed. In rare cases, while our system is still checking available databases, delivery may take longer — we'll email you when your report is ready.
help_faq_4_q: What countries and vehicles are supported?
help_faq_4_a: We support vehicles from all major markets including USA, South Korea, EU, UK, and many more. Any valid 17-character VIN from a recognized manufacturer is supported.
help_faq_5_q: Can I get a refund if no data is found?
help_faq_5_a: Yes. If our provider returns no data for your VIN, you are entitled to a full refund. Contact support with your VIN and order details and we will process it promptly.

country_china_description: China has 350M+ registered vehicles and the world's largest used-car market. Odometer fraud and hidden accident history are common. Check before you buy or import.
country_china_issue_0: Odometer rollback — common on high-mileage domestic and imported cars
country_china_issue_1: Hidden accident repairs — body shop records often don't travel with the vehicle
country_china_issue_2: Salvage & write-off vehicles relisted without full disclosure
country_china_issue_3: Export/import record gaps — cars shipped overseas with incomplete history
country_china_included_4: Odometer rollback detection across service records
country_china_issues_sub: The most common red flags on Chinese used vehicles — before you hand over a deposit.
country_china_included_sub: Every report pulls registration signals, insurance indicators and marketplace data across China's major provinces and export channels.
country_china_included_note: Data is sourced directly from providers — we do not estimate or fabricate records.
country_china_faq_0_q: What does a Chinese VIN starting with 'L' mean?
country_china_faq_0_a: VINs starting with 'L' are assigned to vehicles manufactured in China. It confirms factory origin but does not guarantee a clean history — always check mileage and accident records.
country_china_faq_1_q: Are BYD, Geely and NIO vehicles covered?
country_china_faq_1_a: Yes. Our reports cover major domestic brands including BYD, Geely, NIO, Chery and SAIC, as well as imported vehicles registered in China.
country_china_faq_2_q: Can I check a Chinese car before importing it?
country_china_faq_2_a: Yes. Run a VIN check before export to surface odometer fraud, salvage flags and hidden accident repairs that may not appear in your destination country.
country_china_wwc_mileage_seo: We cross-check odometer readings against national registration signals, service records and marketplace data across China.
country_china_wwc_accidents_seo: We surface collision and insurance claim history — including hidden body repairs often omitted in private sales.
country_china_wwc_salvage_seo: We flag salvage, write-off and rebuilt vehicles — including cars relisted after total-loss declarations.
country_china_wwc_theft_seo: We check theft and recovery records plus export/import signals so cross-border history does not stay hidden.
country_uae_description: The UAE has 3M+ registered vehicles and an import-heavy used market centred on Dubai. Flood imports, odometer rollbacks and GCC registration gaps are common. Check before you buy.
country_uae_issue_0: Flood-damaged imports — US and Japan flood cars retitled in the GCC
country_uae_issue_1: Odometer rollback on luxury imports — Toyota, Nissan and Mercedes are frequent targets
country_uae_issue_2: GCC registration gaps — cars re-registered in Dubai or Abu Dhabi with incomplete prior history
country_uae_issue_3: Hidden US/Japan import damage — auction totals and insurance write-offs not disclosed locally
country_uae_included_4: Odometer rollback detection on imported luxury vehicles
country_uae_included_5: US, Japan and GCC cross-border history signals
country_uae_issues_sub: The most common red flags on UAE used vehicles — before you hand over a deposit.
country_uae_included_sub: Every report pulls registration signals, insurance indicators and import data across Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the wider GCC.
country_uae_included_note: Data is sourced directly from providers — we do not estimate or fabricate records.
country_uae_faq_0_q: Are flood-damaged imports common in Dubai?
country_uae_faq_0_a: Yes. Flood-damaged vehicles from the US and other markets are sometimes imported and sold in Dubai and Abu Dhabi with incomplete disclosure. A VIN check helps surface prior total-loss and flood records.
country_uae_faq_1_q: Does the report cover Toyota, Nissan and Mercedes imports?
country_uae_faq_1_a: Yes. Our reports cover popular UAE imports including Toyota, Nissan, Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Lexus, plus GCC-registered domestic stock.
country_uae_faq_2_q: Can I verify GCC registration history?
country_uae_faq_2_a: Yes. We cross-check UAE and wider GCC registration signals with import and auction data so prior damage and mileage rollbacks are harder to hide.

country_uae_wwc_accidents_seo: We surface collision and insurance claim history — including hidden damage on high-volume import brands.
country_uae_wwc_salvage_seo: We flag flood, salvage and write-off vehicles — including US and Japan imports retitled in the UAE.
country_uae_wwc_theft_seo: We check theft and recovery records plus import signals so cross-border history does not stay hidden.

free_decoder_seo_title: Free VIN decoder for BMW, Audi, Mercedes & more
free_decoder_seo_sub: Decode any 17-character VIN to reveal year, make, model, engine, and factory data. Works for German, Japanese, American, and Korean imports — then unlock mileage and accident history with one full report.
free_decoder_seo_how_sub: Every vehicle identification number follows the ISO 3779 standard. Our decoder reads the WMI, VDS, and VIS sections instantly.
free_decoder_seo_step_0_desc: Type or paste the chassis number from the windshield, door sticker, or registration papers.
free_decoder_seo_step_1_desc: The first three characters reveal the manufacturer — BMW (WBA/WBS), Audi (WAU), Mercedes (WDD), Toyota (JT), and more.
free_decoder_seo_step_2_desc: Characters 4–9 encode model line, body style, engine family, and restraint systems.
free_decoder_seo_step_3_desc: Free decode shows factory specs. The full report adds verified mileage, accidents, salvage, and theft checks.
free_decoder_seo_brands_sub: Tap a brand to try a sample VIN — or paste your own 17-character chassis number above.
free_decoder_brand_bmw_desc: Decode BMW chassis numbers: 3 Series, 5 Series, X5, and M models. WMI codes WBA, WBS, 5UX and German/US plant patterns.
free_decoder_brand_audi_desc: Decode Audi VINs (WAU, TRU). A3, A4, A6, Q5, and RS models — model line, engine code, and assembly plant from the VIN.
free_decoder_brand_mercedes_desc: Decode Mercedes-Benz VINs (WDD, WDB, 4JG). C-Class, E-Class, GLC, and AMG — factory engine and body data from the chassis number.
free_decoder_brand_volkswagen_desc: Decode VW VINs (WVW, 3VW). Golf, Passat, Tiguan, and ID models — WMI, model code, and plant location instantly.
free_decoder_brand_toyota_desc: Decode Toyota and Lexus VINs (JT, 5TD). Camry, Corolla, RAV4 — year, engine, and country of origin from the VIN.
free_decoder_brand_ford_desc: Decode Ford and Lincoln VINs (1FA, 1FT). F-150, Mustang, Explorer — NHTSA-backed specs for US and import vehicles.
free_decoder_brand_honda_desc: Decode Honda and Acura VINs (1HG, JHM). Civic, Accord, CR-V — model year, engine displacement, and assembly plant.
free_decoder_brand_hyundai_desc: Decode Hyundai and Kia VINs (KMH, 5NP). Elantra, Tucson, Santa Fe — essential before importing from Korea.
free_decoder_brand_mazda_desc: Decode Mazda VINs (JM1, JM3, 3MZ, 7MM). Mazda3, CX-5, CX-30, MX-5 — model line and plant from the VIN.
free_decoder_seo_vin_title: What each part of the VIN means
free_decoder_seo_vin_desc: A VIN is not random. Decoders split it into three blocks so you can verify the car matches the listing before you buy.
free_decoder_faq_0_q: What is a free VIN decoder?
free_decoder_faq_0_a: A VIN decoder reads the 17-digit chassis number and returns factory data: year, make, model, engine, and plant. kmcheck offers this free; mileage and accident history require the full report.
free_decoder_faq_1_q: Does it work for BMW and Audi VINs?
free_decoder_faq_1_a: Yes. German WMI prefixes (WBA, WBS, WAU, WDD, WVW) are supported. Paste any BMW, Audi, Mercedes, or VW VIN for instant decode.
free_decoder_faq_2_a: Yes — year, make, model, engine, body, and check digit are free. No subscription. An optional free account may be required during high traffic.
free_decoder_faq_3_q: How is this different from a full VIN report?
free_decoder_faq_3_a: The decoder shows factory specs from the VIN structure. The full report cross-checks mileage, accidents, salvage titles, and theft from insurance and registration databases.
free_decoder_seo_cta_title: Factory specs are free. History is one click away.
free_decoder_seo_cta_desc: After decoding, unlock verified odometer readings, accident records, and salvage status — usually within seconds.
help_faq_6_a: All payments are processed securely by PayPal. We never store your card details. You can pay with any major card or your PayPal account.
